motion: Is the evolutionary argument against naturalism successful at showing that naturalism plus evolution gives its believers a defeater for trusting their cognitive faculties?

burdenRoutes.description: Establish that naturalism plus evolution rationally defeats confidence in cognitive reliability and thereby defeats itself.
burdenRoutes.successCriteria: Support the low reliability probability premise, the reliability defeater, and its extension to naturalism plus evolution.

bridges.description: Connect the reliability defeater back to rational acceptance of naturalism plus evolution.
Show that adaptive neurological success does not select belief content for truth.
Clarify naturalism, materialism, cognitive reliability, or the scope of the conclusion.

burdenRoutes.description: Show that evolution can favor true belief or that the proposed reliability problem does not uniquely support the EAAN.
burdenRoutes.successCriteria: Defend a behavior-to-content constraint or establish a parallel skeptical difficulty for the proposed theistic alternative.

bridges.description: Undercut the claimed rational self-defeat of naturalism plus evolution.
Connect adaptive behavior and desires to selection for generally true belief content.
Clarify the EAAN conclusion or compare its skeptical implications with theism.

source.limitations: YouTube auto-generated English captions contain occasional lexical errors; selected turns have clear named or uninterrupted turn ownership and therefore high attribution confidence.

inventoryProtocol.selectionStatement: Twelve chronological single-speaker acts were selected from the complete substantive exchange: two constructive acts per side and eight direct responsive acts.
